name: Fertiliser supply
value: Hormuz closed to Gulf urea exports
summary: Gulf urea exports still stuck behind Hormuz in the conflict's ninth month
state: Hormuz, the route for about a third of world urea exports, remains largely closed (Global Agriculture, 30 Oct; IFPRI). US retail urea was $674 a ton in mid-October, 13% higher than a year earlier, as Chinese exports offset some of the loss. A key export route closed meets the Alert line; the IRGC's 4 Nov mine claims add to the risk.
for_you: Farmers face higher fertiliser costs, which can feed into food prices next season. Import-dependent countries in South Asia and Africa are most exposed.

sources.title: Global Agriculture — Fertiliser costs stay high as Hormuz conflict drags into ninth month
IFPRI — How are fertilizer markets coping with the continued closure of Hormuz?
CNBC — The Hormuz blockage is rattling fertilizer markets

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
